rows.summary:
DeepfakeHTTP is an MIT-licensed, single-jar Java web server. It answers requests by matching them against plain-text HTTP request/response dumps. Its README lists REST and GraphQL API mocking and testing, PoCs and demos, and HTTP tinkering as its uses. That gives testers a useful, low-setup way to stand up a stubbed backend, which the pinned README doesn't otherwise offer. rows.summary: The PR adds one line to Test Automation Frameworks: "[bareenv](https://github.com/Blasword/bareenv) - Runs a command once per environment combination (unset, empty, invalid) and reports the ones that break." The repository README backs this up. bareenv is an MIT-licensed Node CLI and GitHub Action. It reruns a command with chosen environment variables unset, empty or set to an invalid path. It then sorts each run into verdicts such as env-dependent, expected-fail and not-observed, and prints a command to reproduce each failure. It can also compare a report against an earlier run so a PR fails only on new findings. The pinned README lists no tool for this kind of environment-variable robustness testing, and no earlier submission in the history index mentions it. The entry ends with a period, follows the entry format, and is a single-item PR, so it meets the written rules. Two things are judgment calls, not rule violations. First, bareenv is a test runner/utility rather than a framework, but Bats (a shell testing tool) is the closest neighbour and no better section exists. Second, the project is very new: 0 stars, 11 commits, v0.1.0, and no npm package. The maintainer has turned down 'too niche' (#107) and unproven (#288) entries before. My tentative recommendation is approve, with the maintainer deciding whether it clears the bar.
